subject: Follow-up: capacity commitments, hyperscaler comparison, and proposed test scope
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: capacity commitments, hyperscaler comparison, and proposed test scope

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: low-latency customer support NLU + reranker for search. Typical request is 512 tokens max, avg 120 tokens.
- Current pain: unpredictable tail latency and large per-token costs on the hyperscaler managed endpoints.
- Procurement timeline: goal to pilot in June and finalize procurement by end of Q3.

What we propose for the pilot/test:
1) A 2-week controlled comparison between: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) vs. hyperscaler reserved GPU instances (customer-managed).
   - Goal metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost/token, and availability under load.
2) Test matrix attached (FINLYTICS_redwood-test-matrix.xlsx) with workload shapes (burst, steady-state), sequence lengths, and concurrency points.
3) Redwood will provision a dedicated GPU pool sized to match your target QPS for the pilot and provide a reserved capacity agreement for the 2-week window.

Questions / asks for you:
- Confirm the test window (we suggested Jun 1–14 but flexible).
- Confirm hyperscaler instance types you want to compare (we typically see A100 / H100 / G5/V100 equivalents).
- Any compliance gating (SOC 2 evidence / IP restrictions) we should surface to legal/procurement now.

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm procurement contact and preferred test dates.
- We push a short SOW and test plan for signatures.
- Vanessa will reach out to align on the runbook and provisioning timeline.

Attachments: FINLYTICS_redwood-test-matrix.xlsx (test matrix)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15m sync if easier.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice.park@finlytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T20:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capacity commitments, hyperscaler comparison, and proposed test scope

Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. The plan looks good; Jun 1–14 works for our engineering calendar. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement needs an initial SOW + estimated pilot cost. Can Redwood provide a one-page price estimate and the SOW draft?
- Hyperscaler side: we’ll compare against GCP A2 (and a smaller A100 profile) — I can confirm exact instance sizes after checking with infra.
- Compliance: we do require SOC 2 Type II evidence for pilots that touch customer data. Can you point us to our security contact?

Also, we need clarification on what you mean by “reserved capacity agreement” — does that require a monetary commitment up front or can it be time-bound with guaranteed capacity without a spend commitment?

I’ll loop procurement (procurement@finlytics.com) if you can send SOW + price estimate.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Head of Product
FinLytics
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capacity commitments, hyperscaler comparison, and proposed test scope

Alice —

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation and procurement questions. Short answers here and details below. We’ll also attach a short one-page comparison PDF and SOW draft in this thread (see attachments).

Reserved capacity explanation:
- For the pilot we can offer a time-bound reserved capacity commitment (no long-term monetary lock) that guarantees the dedicated pool size for the agreed test dates. If you move to production and want a discounted reserved contract, that would be a separate commercial commitment (monthly/annual).

Pilot pricing model options:
- Option A (no upfront commit): short-term reserved pool enabled for the test window, billed for actual usage at a pilot rate (higher than committed pricing).
- Option B (short-term commitment): small prepaid commit for the pilot (credit applied to usage) — this reduces unit token costs for the pilot and guarantees capacity.

Security / Compliance:
- SOC 2 Type II report available; I’ve included a link to our security page in the SOW. Vanessa will introduce our security contact if you need direct evidence.

Proposed test details (from the attachment):
- Models: the same open model on both environments (fp16 baseline). We can run additional quantized variants (int8) as a secondary axis.
- Measurement points:
   * Cold start latencies (first token after idle)
   * Steady-state tail latencies (p95/p99 over 10k requests)
   * Throughput under batching (tokens/sec with batching turned on)
   * Preemption/resilience: we’ll simulate noisy neighbor events on hyperscaler instances where feasible
- Target KPIs to validate: p99 < 250ms for 512 token requests under target concurrency; cost/token delta between environments; failover behavior under capacity pressure.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-one-pager.pdf, SOW_FinLytics_Pilot_v1.docx, FINLYTICS_redwood-test-matrix.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) We send the SOW + 1-pager price estimate to procurement (I’ll do that today).
2) Vanessa will reach out to schedule provisioning prep and a pre-test checklist call.
3) Confirm hyperscaler instance sizes (Alice).

If that reads OK I’ll route the SOW for signature and we’ll provision the dedicated pool for Jun 1.

— Logan
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finlytics.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capacity commitments, hyperscaler comparison, and proposed test scope

Hi Alice / Logan —

I’ll own the runbook and the provisioning activity for the pilot. A few technical clarifications so we can size and instrument properly: 

Instrumentation & measurements:
- We’ll provide Prometheus / Grafana dashboards with the following metrics: per-token latency histograms, GPU utilization, memory residency (KV cache warming), request QPS, and error rates.
- Test harness: we recommend running both steady-state (30m windows) and burst windows (5m) across 3 sequence-length buckets (64, 128, 512).

Sizing & config notes:
- Batch sizes to test: {auto-batching, manual batch 8, 16}.
- KV cache warm: run a warm-up phase of 20k tokens before steady-state measurement.
- Quantization: baseline runs in fp16, then int8 quantized runs to show cost/latency trade-offs.

Hyperscaler specifics to confirm from FinLytics:
- Exact instance families (GCP A2, A100 variants, or AWS p4d/p4de). We need their expected QPS per instance to mirror capacity.

Fall-back and routing test:
- Redwood can run canary fallback tests where requests are automatically routed to a lower-cost instance type under load or to a fallback model variant; we’ll include a failover test to validate reliability during noisy-neighbor events.

Runbook deliverables:
- Pre-test checklist and provisioning timeline (48–72h provisioning lead time for dedicated pool).
- Measurement dashboard link.
- Post-test report with cost-normalized comparisons and recommendation.

I’ll await the confirmed hyperscaler instance sizes and procurement sign-off.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Procurement here. A few items we need before we can sign the SOW:

Regards,
